newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate OKs bill for levy repairs, ballpark.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate OKs bill for levy repairs, ballpark.

text.p: California's state Senate on Thursday approved legislation that would speed levy repairs statewide and help San Francisco build a new ballpark, lawmakers said.
The Senate approved the legislation by a vote of 37-to-0.
A spokesman for Gov. Pete Wilson said the governor intended to sign the legislation, which was approved by the state Assembly earlier this week.
Senate Bill 181, by Senator Quentin Kopp, would provide targeted exemptions from the California Environmental Quality Act to speed flood-damage repairs in the state.

The bill would provide similar exemptions to a proposed major league ballpark for the San Francisco Giants. Proponents of the bill said it would speed the ballpark construction timeline by three to four months.

The ballpark, which is scheduled to open in April of 2000, will cost about $255 million to build. The financing package includes $10 million in tax increment financing by the San Francisco Redevelopment Agency.
Senate Bill 181 was introduced specifically to help San Francisco build the new ballpark, but it was amended by state lawmakers to speed flood recovery efforts.
